clue.text: Facts not sure, but might possibly be found in comestibles

indicators.note: what these words might possibly be is a rearrangement of them, so their letters are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doubtful set of facts that might turn up in food, like an allergy warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might possibly be' signals rearranging FACTS NOT SURE. The definition reads as a description: these are what food labels warn may be found in eatables.
explanation.definitionFit: Allergen warnings on packaged food say it may contain small amounts of nuts, things found within eatables.

clue.text: Lake is hot with discolouration

parts.note: a tarn is a small mountain lake
taken as written
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A lake's water is warm and stained.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun the word means a dulling stain or loss of lustre, a discolouring of metal.

clue.text: Endless metallic sculpture, ever since the big bang

indicators.note: a sculpture is something shaped and moulded, so the letters are reformed into a new arrangement
endless means the last letter of the word metallic is cut off

explanation.surface: An unfinished metal sculpture said to be the greatest since the universe began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' removes C from METALLIC, leaving METALLI; 'sculpture' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-time record is the greatest ever, so the phrase loosely spans the whole of history since creation.

clue.text: Happy Geri upset to see the writing on the wall

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cheerful pop singer distressed by what she reads as a bad omen.
explanation.walkthrough: Geri suggests Geri Halliwell of the Spice Girls; 'the writing on the wall' sounds like a portent but is meant literally: inscriptions.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of inscriptions, words carved or written on walls and monuments, is this discipline.

clue.text: Alternative that's given to a student in college

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
that is, abbreviated i.e.
L is a learner, as on a British learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: Another option offered to an undergraduate within the college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for 'that is', i.e. Oriel is an Oxford college.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriel is one of the colleges of Oxford University, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Posh type, one keeping affected manner in foreign capital

indicators.note: keeping means holding inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: a nob is a toff, a posh person
an air is an affected manner, as in putting on airs
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A snob with pretentious airs abroad in a far-off capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foreign capital' is the definition; 'Posh type' is the British slang 'nob' for a toff, and 'keeping' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, a capital abroad from the setter's British viewpoint.

clue.text: Meal got up to be a bloomer

parts.note: tea is a light afternoon or evening meal in Britain
rose is the past tense of rise, to get up

explanation.surface: A meal goes up in the world and becomes a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a mistake, but here it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea rose is a variety of rose, a flowering plant, i.e. something that blooms.

clue.text: Companies endlessly talk about a menace in stores

indicators.note: about signals the letters are moved around and rearranged
endlessly means the word companies loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Businesses complain constantly about a threat in their shops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' drops S from COMPANIES; 'about' rearranges COMPANIE with TALK.
explanation.definitionFit: A compulsive thief is a menace to shops, where they pocket goods.

clue.text: Siren broke 4 over European article

indicators.note: over means covering, so the rearranged letters wrap around the article
broke means smashed, so the letters of that answer are rearranged

parts.note: refers to the answer at 4 down, the Oxford college Oriel
le is the French definite article

explanation.surface: A siren broke a college window above a European object.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 refers to the answer at 4 down; 'broke' rearranges it and 'over', in an across clue, means wrapping round.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is a Rhine maiden of legend who lured sailors to their doom, like a siren.

clue.text: Create an impression?

parts.note: an impressionist creates an impression of someone by copying them

explanation.definitionFit: To copy someone's manner is to do an impression of them, as mimics do.

clue.text: Their signs may be seen where eastern country has a loo

parts.note: a state is a country
the Gents is a British name for a men's toilet

explanation.surface: Signs of a property firm are spotted where an Eastern country has a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their signs' points to the For Sale boards property sellers put up outside houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Property agents put For Sale signs outside the houses they are selling, so their signs may be seen.

clue.text: Promotion less heated but more costly

parts.note: PR is public relations, promoting a product or person
icier means colder, less heated

explanation.surface: A promotion with less excitement turns out more expensive.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dearer costs more money, a straightforward comparative synonym.

clue.text: Observer finds nothing right in a bumpkin

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these go within the other word

parts.note: a lout is an oafish, uncouth fellow
O is zero, nothing
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A watcher discovers nothing correct about a country yokel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right' as OK rather than R is the trap; 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentry posted to keep watch is one who observes.

clue.text: Colour-blending chore

indicators.note: blending mixes things together, so the letters are combined in a new order

explanation.surface: Mixing paint colours is a tedious task.
explanation.definitionFit: Ochre is a yellowish-brown earth pigment and shade.

clue.text: Head at hand keeping the same

indicators.note: keeping means holding within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: present means here, at hand
id. is the abbreviation of idem, Latin for the same

explanation.surface: A leader who stays close by and doesn't change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the same' is the scholarly abbreviation id. (idem); 'keeping' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A president is the head of a state, college or organisation.

clue.text: Gentle lay, rendered with style

indicators.note: rendered means made into, so these letters are re-made in a new order

explanation.surface: A soft song performed with grace.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something gracefully and stylishly is to do it in this manner.

clue.text: Jaguar follows supreme original model

indicators.note: follows means one piece comes after the other

parts.note: arch means chief or supreme, as in archenemy
the E-Type is a classic Jaguar sports car

explanation.surface: A big cat trailing behind the top original pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jaguar' suggests the animal but is the car maker.
explanation.definitionFit: An archetype is the first pattern from which copies are made, the prototype.

clue.text: One starts a sentence — sentence ended here

definitions.meaning: ... punishment ends a death sentence with execution

explanation.surface: A grammar note and a prison note in one breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The second 'sentence' turns from grammar to the courtroom: a capital sentence ends in death.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: an upper-case letter opens a sentence, and execution concludes a death sentence.

clue.text: Old record — one volume gives a typical example

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record, an old format
I is the Roman numeral one
a tome is a large book or volume

explanation.surface: An old record and a single book provide a classic specimen.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect embodiment of a type is a model instance.

clue.text: Point where stupor grips many?

indicators.note: grips means holds inside, so one piece is contained by the other

parts.note: a coma is a deep stupor
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, i.e. many

explanation.surface: Asking at what stage a numbness takes hold of many people.
explanation.definitionFit: A comma is a punctuation mark, and punctuation marks are known as points.

clue.text: Fancy having accord with soldiers!

parts.note: to chime with is to agree or accord
RA is the Royal Artillery, a British army regiment

explanation.surface: An exclamation at being in agreement with the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A chimera is a wild imaginative fancy, an illusion of the mind.

clue.text: Control of teacher variable?

parts.note: a schoolmaster is a teacher
Y is a common variable in algebra

explanation.surface: A question of how much command a changeable teacher has.
explanation.definitionFit: Command or expert skill over something is mastery, a synonym.

clue.text: Setter's volume includes right to show publisher's identity

parts.note: the setter is I, so the setter's = I am, I'm

indicators.note: includes means contains, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: a pint is a measure of volume

explanation.surface: A crossword maker's book carries a correction showing who published it.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaking of themselves is a crossword convention; 'includes' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A book's imprint is the publisher's name printed on it, identifying the firm.

clue.text: Rate of return for work with police

indicators.note: return means turn back, so the whole combination is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: Asking what speed a return to work with the police would be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns OPMET to read the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempo is the speed or pace of something, especially music.

clue.text: Sneeze said to be in dispute?

indicators.note: said means spoken, so it is how the word sounds that counts

parts.note: atishoo is the British spelling of the sound of a sneeze

explanation.surface: A sneeze, it is claimed, is arguable.
explanation.definitionFit: A matter under discussion or argument is in question, a phrase synonym.

clue.text: Sergeant major of marines after his share of the grub?

indicators.note: after means coming behind, so the officer and marines follow the share

parts.note: a cut is a share, as of profits
a sergeant major is a warrant officer, WO
RM is the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A senior marine soldier wants his share of the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' sounds like food but is a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A cutworm is a moth caterpillar, i.e. a grub that cuts through plant stems.

clue.text: English capital in danger at a certain point

indicators.note: in means placed within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a threat is a danger

indicators.note: capital means the leading letter, so the first letter of English is used

explanation.surface: England's capital city in peril at some specific moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'English capital' looks like London but is just E; 'in' puts it inside THREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereat is an old word meaning at that place or at that moment.

clue.text: Dependent on charity, it makes Moseley yearn to be free

indicators.note: letters set free are released from their order and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something makes a man named Moseley long for freedom, relying on handouts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes alms-giving, so it relates to or depends on charitable gifts.
